# **Principal Quantitative and Architecture Audit: Local NSE F\&O Decision Cockpit for an External IDE-Agent CIO**

This local paper-trading cockpit should become a deterministic, fail-closed market-telemetry and risk-envelope kernel that hands an external IDE agent—Codex, Antigravity, Claude, or another agent—a compact, provenance-verified market picture for independent discretionary judgment. It must never become an uncalibrated indicator dump, a prose-rationale grading theater, or an autonomous trade-execution loop. Working strictly from the supplied dossier—with zero access to the repository, database, broker adapter, or live market feed—the system is **not validated for live capital and should not be trusted for further paper-performance evaluation until Phase 0 accounting, whole-lot sizing, dual-stop, and data-provenance controls are built and verified**.  
The central quantitative blocker is the contradiction between an apparently strong historical paper-ledger summary and the current-regime logic-test slice of 31 trades, 19.4% win rate, profit factor 0.15, and net loss of −₹33,8091. Exact algebraic reconstruction isolates 6 wins and 25 losses, gross profit of approximately ₹5,966 (₹5,734–₹6,202 across profit-factor rounding from 0.145 to 0.155), gross loss of approximately ₹39,775 (₹39,543–₹40,011), an average win of ₹994 against an average loss of ₹1,591 (an inverted 0.625× payoff ratio), and expectancy of −₹1,091 per trade—erasing 67.6% of the ₹50,000 paper budget1. Assuming independent trials, observing 6 or fewer wins in 31 trades carries a one-sided exact binomial probability of 0.27% against a 45% baseline win rate (4.6% against 35%; exact 95% confidence interval: 7.5%–37.5%), and at a 0.625× payoff ratio, even raising the win rate to 45% would yield a profit factor of only 0.51 while breakeven demands 61.5%1. Official empirical priors reinforce this skepticism: SEBI's August 2026 study of FY2025–26 individual equity-derivatives accounts reports that 87.7% incurred net losses (₹91,685 crore aggregate net losses; 92% in options; roughly ₹25,000 crore in transaction costs), while 99% of FPI and proprietary trading profits accrued to algorithmic entities2.

Because no source files, schemas, historical ledgers, or broker logs were inspected, every conclusion in this review explicitly separates dossier facts from working assumptions and unresolved unknowns.

## **1\. Executive Verdict: What This System Should Become and Must Never Become**

* **Become a deterministic, fail-closed perception and risk-envelope kernel.** The local software must verify data provenance, enforce non-negotiable capital and stop invariants, compute no-arbitrage pricing and late-2026 NSE frictions, and expose clean bounded state to the external IDE agent.  
* **Become an adversarial realism simulator before counting any paper edge.** Every simulated fill must cross live ask/bid depth (failing closed when unavailable), apply decision-to-arrival latency and Stop-Loss Limit (SL-L) stop slippage, deduct post-April 2026 Indian statutory charges (0.15% sell-side STT, 0.03553% NSE charges including IPFT, SEBI fee, stamp duty, 18% GST, and brokerage), and log Perold implementation shortfall16.  
* **Become a polarity-typed dual-stop safety enforcer.** The local kernel must enforce monotonically non-decreasing option-premium catastrophic stops for both long calls and long puts, enforce opposite-polarity monotonic underlying-forward invalidation (non-decreasing floor for long calls; non-increasing ceiling for long puts), and run pre-entry Black-76 theta/IV-crush stress validation1.  
* **Become a lean, context-budgeted MCP decision surface.** Empirical findings on long-context attention decay ("lost in the middle") and non-additive modality noise in LLM trading agents argue for a minimal \~30-field decision packet with hard constraints anchored at the top and bottom rather than sprawling option chains or fundamental dumps19.  
* **Become a pre-registered statistical testbed for agentic judgment.** Every session must log the exact IDE model identifier, prompt hash, schema version, invocation mode, and volatility regime so out-of-sample evaluation can apply Bailey–López de Prado Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) and Politis–Romano stationary bootstrap tests across at least 150–275+ closed trades1.  
* **Never become an autonomous entry, trailing, or discretionary-exit loop.** Signals must remain read-only evidence; all discretionary trade proposals must originate from the external IDE agent, restricting local background authority solely to evidence refresh, fail-closed gating, hard emergency stop enforcement, and deterministic end-of-day (EOD) square-off.  
* **Never become a "500-signal" telemetry dump or prose-rationale verification theater.** NeurIPS 2023 and Anthropic's May 2025 chain-of-thought (CoT) faithfulness experiments show models frequently omit true causal influences from verbal explanations (20% faithfulness for Claude 3.7 Sonnet and 29% for DeepSeek R1 on misaligned-hint tests, degrading further on harder problems)23, while Goodhart's Law turns prose checklists into reward-hacking targets25.  
* **Never permit single-trade risk to equal the daily loss limit alongside multi-position concurrency.** Sizing at ₹3,500 per trade (7.0% of ₹50,000) across two concurrent positions creates a ₹7,000 (14.0%) correlated gap-risk tail and a 23.3% probability of halving capital over 100 trades *even under a genuine \+0.125R positive expectancy*1.  
* **Never treat delayed, provisional, or non-trading sources as live execution truth.** Intraday NSE open interest updates only every 1–3 minutes and remains provisional until evening settlement27, US-style dealer gamma assumptions misclassify India's predominantly retail option-buying market28, and NSE Market Lens and NSE's official MCP portal explicitly restrict usage to information and learning rather than live or virtual trading31.  
* **Never enable live trading through a configuration switch.** Live NSE deployment requires strict adherence to SEBI's April 1, 2026 retail-algo regime (whitelisted static IP, OAuth \+ 2FA, compulsory daily logout, ≤10 orders/second Algo ID tagging, 5-year audit retention, and NSE's pre-emptive ban on algorithmic market orders) alongside daily human arming, idempotent IN\_DOUBT timeout reconciliation, Limit Price Protection (LPP) / SL-L handling, and broker-side plus marketable-limit emergency exit ladders32.

![][image1]  
Taken together, the three diagnostic layers explain why patching individual trading rules before fixing measurement and risk mechanics is premature. First, the 31-trade loss reflects dual failure—both low directional accuracy and a 0.625× payoff inversion where winners averaged ₹994 while losers averaged ₹1,591, consistent with premature profit-taking, option theta/spread erosion, or slipped stops1. Second, even if a repaired workflow achieves a strong \+0.125R net expectancy (45% win rate at 1.5R payoff), fixed ₹3,500 sizing (7.0% of budget) produces a 41.0% median maximum drawdown, a 98.5% 95th-percentile maximum drawdown, and a 4.9% wipeout rate over 100 trades; dropping risk to ₹1,500 (3.0%) cuts the ≥50% drawdown probability from 23.3% to 2.8% and wipeout probability to 0.0%1. Third, an illustrative 100-trade, 2-lot NIFTY simulation demonstrates that realistic late-2026 NSE friction—0.75 pt entry drag, 0.75 pt winner exit drag, 2.5 pt SL-L stop-exit slippage, and ₹84.19/round-trip statutory plus ₹20/order brokerage charges—extracts ₹39,749 (flipping a \+₹29,120 naive paper profit to −₹10,629), expanding to ₹65,587 drag (−₹36,467 net) if optimistic touch-fill assumptions also overstate win rate by 5 percentage points1.

Raise PARITY\_ANOMALY if ![][image52] of spot, catching broken chain quotes automatically. **Counterargument and failure mode:** On final-hour Tuesday expiry or wide spreads, parity noise rises slightly; fall back to carry-adjusted active futures only when dispersion exceeds tolerance, tagging precision as degraded. **Manipulation, overfitting, and staleness:** Zero free parameters—pure no-arbitrage pricing; staleness arises only if expiry calendar or holiday ![][image47] calculation drifts. **Rejection criterion:** Reject engine calibration if ATM Call and Put implied volatilities diverge by \>0.5 vol pts under normal liquidity. **Control class, cost, and value vs. risk:** **Advisory evidence engine** (supplies Upgrade 4's hard stress gate); **Medium** implementation cost; high decision value with minimal false-confidence risk.

### **Upgrade 8 (Phase 1): Pre-Trade Friction-to-Risk Ratio (FRR) and Depth Participation Liquidity Gate**

**Exact problem solved:** Replaces vague "spread looks wide" discretion with a capital-calibrated liquidity filter that blocks entries whenever crossing spreads and statutory costs consume an unrecoverable share of risk budget1. **Data required and provenance/freshness:** Live L1 bid/ask prices and L1 bid/ask quantities (rolling 5-second window, age ≤ 1 s), intended quantity ![][image3] (units), planned risk ![][image53] (₹), and Upgrade 1's ![][image10] (₹). **Mathematical specification and 6-part validation:** Define Friction-to-Risk Ratio (FRR, %) and Depth Participation Ratio (DPR, dimensionless) as:  
![][image54]  
*Calibration:* On 1-lot NIFTY (65 units, ![][image55]), a ₹0.50 spread produces FRR \= 5.6%, ₹1.50 produces 9.3%, ₹3.00 produces 14.9%, and ₹6.00 produces 26.0%1. Hard initial gates: rolling 5-second median FRR ≤ 12.0% and rolling 5-second median DPR ≤ 0.25 (at least 4× order size resting at touch). *Null hypothesis (![][image56]):* Net fee-adjusted expectancy for trades entering at FRR \> 12% or DPR \> 0.25 equals or exceeds trades meeting both gates. *Robustness test:* Walk-forward sensitivity across FRR ∈ {8%, 10%, 12%, 15%} and DPR ∈ {0.15, 0.25, 0.50} on recorded live ticks must show monotonic reduction in realized implementation shortfall without starving liquid ATM setups. *Superiority over simpler evidence:* Raw spread in rupees or % of premium ignores lot multipliers, fixed ₹47.20 brokerage+GST drag, and stop width—a ₹1.50 spread is manageable on a 40-pt stop but destructive on a 10-pt stop, while DPR prevents walking thin books even when the top tick briefly looks narrow1. **Counterargument and failure mode:** Fleeting market-maker quotes can flicker below thresholds momentarily (addressed by the 5-second rolling median). **Manipulation, overfitting, and staleness:** The CIO could artificially widen the stop to inflate ![][image53] and lower FRR; Upgrade 3's ![][image43] ceiling and Upgrade 4's structural stress gate close this loophole. **Rejection criterion:** Recalibrate thresholds if rolling FRR/DPR blocks \>30% of liquid ATM NIFTY regular-session ticks, or if accepted trades routinely incur realized IS \> 1.5× modeled FRR. **Control class, cost, and value vs. risk:** **Hard safety control**; **Low** implementation cost; high decision and safety value with very low false-confidence risk.

### **Upgrade 9 (Phase 1): Deterministic Numeric Fact-Binding Validator and P\&L-Blind In-Trade Framing**

**Exact problem solved:** Catches LLM perception/copy hallucinations (wrong strike, stale quote, arithmetic mismatch91) and curbs disposition-effect and sunk-cost anchoring during trade management—without deploying broken semantic CoT checking23. **Data required and provenance/freshness:** The immutable frozen packet\_id snapshot (age ≤ 15 s) and the CIO's structured entry/management proposal payload. **Falsifiable definition and formula (with units):** Pre-trade deterministic validator rejects any proposal (SCHEMA\_FACT\_REJECT) where packet\_id age exceeds 15 s, where any cited quote differs from the frozen snapshot by \>1 tick (₹0.05) or \>0.05% on index levels, or where stated max\_loss\_rs deviates from kernel calculation by \>₹25. For open-position management reviews, the cockpit serves a **P\&L-blind packet** hiding entry price, unrealized rupee P\&L, and multi-day account P\&L, surfacing instead current market structure, distance to invalidation (points), distance to catastrophic stop (₹), coarsened R-multiple bucket (\<0R, 0–1R, 1–2R, \>2R), and live theta burn63. **Counterargument and failure mode:** Masking exact entry price can interfere with trailing-to-breakeven rules if the CIO expects exact cost-basis thresholds; including the coarsened R-bucket (and testing blind vs. R-visible in A/B replay) balances hygiene against management utility. **Manipulation, overfitting, and staleness:** An agent can copy numbers verbatim to pass numeric binding while still making poor directional choices; therefore treat fact-binding strictly as perception hygiene, never reasoning proof. **Rejection criterion:** Never reject deterministic numeric binding (zero downside); drop P\&L-blind framing only if ≥100-trade A/B replay shows blind framing lowers realized payoff ratio or profit factor vs. full-P\&L framing. **Control class, cost, and value vs. risk:** Numeric fact-binding \= **Hard safety control**; P\&L-blind framing \= **Advisory framing control**; **Low** implementation cost; high hygiene value while deliberately avoiding prose-checker false confidence24.

### **Upgrade 10 (Phase 1): Post-Loss Cooldown, Daily Trade-Frequency Cap, and Same-Direction Re-Entry Lockout**

**Exact problem solved:** Blocks Coval–Shumway post-loss risk escalation72, revenge re-entry in choppy ranges, and SEBI-documented high-turnover fee attrition on small capital16. **Data required and provenance/freshness:** Append-only intraday session ledger (age \= 0 ms), stop-out timestamps, and post-stop synthetic-forward price extremes. **Falsifiable definition and formula (with units):** Three persisted account-level hard gates: (1) maximum **3** round-trip trades per day (capping explicit statutory+brokerage drag at roughly ₹200–₹260/day on 1–2 lots); (2) **20-minute** entry lockout after 1 losing trade, escalating to **full-session entry lockout** after 2 losing trades or cumulative intraday realized loss ≥ ₹1,750 (50% of daily cap); and (3) **45-minute** same-direction re-entry lockout on the same underlying after a stop-out unless ![][image28] clears the entry-to-stop extreme by ≥ 0.25 × 15-minute ATR (index points). **Counterargument and failure mode:** Rigid lockouts can miss valid second-attempt breakouts after liquidity sweeps and slow down paper-sample collection. **Manipulation, overfitting, and staleness:** Restarting the app or switching to a correlated index could bypass weak timers; persist state on disk across restarts and enforce caps account-wide. **Rejection criterion:** Log every cooldown-blocked CIO intent as a shadow counterfactual; relax or remove a specific lockout if ≥100 blocked counterfactuals across ≥2 regimes show statistically positive net expectancy (\> \+0.10R, p \< 0.05). **Control class, cost, and value vs. risk:** **Hard safety control** (subject to counterfactual falsification); **Low** implementation cost; high behavioral protection with medium false-confidence risk if lower activity is mistaken for positive edge.

### **Upgrade 11 (Phase 1): Nonlinear Options MAE/MFE and Greek/Implementation-Shortfall Post-Mortem Attribution**

**Exact problem solved:** Pinpoints why the 31-trade slice exhibited a 0.625× payoff inversion and 19.4% win rate by separating directional skill from timing, theta decay, IV crush, basis shift, and execution drag1. **Data required and provenance/freshness:** 1-minute (or tick-sampled) option bid/ask, ![][image28], and Black-76 Greeks archived for every open position from entry through exit plus 30 minutes post-exit. **Mathematical specification and 6-part validation:** Compute exact option-bid excursions ![][image57] (₹), ![][image58] (₹), winner Capture Ratio ![][image59], Perold IS breakdown (₹)18, and second-order Taylor-Greek P\&L attribution summed across 1-minute steps:  
![][image60]  
*Calibration:* Pure accounting identity (unexplained residual ![][image61] directly audits pricing accuracy; target ![][image62] of gross move). *Null hypothesis (![][image56]):* Trade losses stem purely from adverse Delta direction rather than Theta bleed, Vega crush, stop-whipsaw, or implementation shortfall. *Robustness test:* Verify stability separately across 0–1 DTE (gamma/theta-dominated) vs. 3–7 DTE (vega-sensitive) cohorts and inspect 30-minute post-exit counterfactual MFE to detect premature stops. *Superiority over simpler evidence:* Classic Sweeney equity MAE/MFE93 assumes linear 1:1 underlying sensitivity; on options, a trader can be right on direction yet lose to IV crush or sideways theta decay—only Greek attribution separates directional error from strike/expiry selection error. **Counterargument and failure mode:** Post-mortem MAE/MFE tables tempt operators into curve-fitting stops and targets to historical noise. **Manipulation, overfitting, and staleness:** Tuning stop rules every 15 trades invalidates out-of-sample statistics; forbid parameter changes outside pre-registered 50-trade review checkpoints logged as new DSR trials. **Rejection criterion:** Reject the Greek attribution engine if unexplained residual ![][image61] exceeds 20% of gross move on \>15% of trades. **Control class, cost, and value vs. risk:** **Advisory diagnostic only** (offline post-session); **Medium** implementation cost; high diagnostic value with medium overfitting/false-confidence risk if abused for hindsight tuning.

### **Upgrade 12 (Phase 1): Weighted Top-10 Nifty Contribution and India-Honest Provisional OI/GEX Framing**

**Exact problem solved:** Corrects unweighted breadth illusions on concentrated Indian indices (top 10 stocks \= 52%–54.5% of Nifty 5059) and eliminates US-style dealer-GEX sign-inversion traps28. **Data required and provenance/freshness:** Live cash LTP for top-10 Nifty constituents (age ≤ 2 s), quarterly NSE Nifty 50 free-float weights59, Nifty 50 advance/decline counts, intraday chain OI \+ Black-76 Gamma, and NSE prior-EOD participant-wise OI (T-1 trading day28). **Mathematical specification and 6-part validation:** Define Heavyweight Contribution Index ![][image63] (%) and Breadth-Contribution Divergence ![][image64] (dimensionless in \[−1, \+1\]) as:  
![][image65]  
Positive BCD indicates broad confirmation; negative BCD flags narrow heavyweight divergence. Pair with **Unsigned Concentrated Gamma Strikes** (top 2 Call OI×Gamma and Put OI×Gamma strikes in ₹ crore per 1% index move) explicitly tagged PROVISIONAL with OI\_AGE\_SEC and accompanied by prior-EOD NSE Client/Pro/FII net option positioning28. *Calibration:* Uses official quarterly NSE free-float weights with zero fitted statistical parameters59. *Null hypothesis (![][image56]):* Intraday index continuation accuracy is identical when BCD \< 0 vs. BCD \> 0\. *Robustness test:* Split out-of-sample across Financial-Services-led sessions vs. IT/Energy rotation sessions over ≥60 trading days. *Superiority over simpler evidence:* Unweighted 50-stock advance/decline treats HDFC Bank (10.5%–10.6% weight) equally to HDFC Life (0.53%–0.54% weight)—a \~20:1 weighting error59—while unsigned gamma walls plus EOD participant context remove the explicit sign-inversion fallacy of naive US GEX in India28. **Counterargument and failure mode:** Prior-EOD participant OI misses intraday institutional reversals, and constituent weights drift \~0.5%–1.5% between quarterly rebalances59. **Manipulation, overfitting, and staleness:** Missed evening downloads leave EOD positioning stale; enforce strict as\_of\_date \== T-1 gating. **Rejection criterion:** Drop HCI/BCD from the minimal decision packet if ≥100-trade ablation shows zero improvement in directional accuracy or STAND\_ASIDE quality over simple futures price action plus India VIX. **Control class, cost, and value vs. risk:** **Advisory evidence upgrade**; **Medium** implementation cost; medium–high decision value that lowers false-confidence risk by exposing structural uncertainty honestly.

## **4\. Phased Implementation Roadmap**

### **Phase 0: Fix Before Trusting More Paper Results**

No additional paper trades should count toward proving edge until Upgrades **U1 through U5** pass unit, property-based, and replay validation. Together, Phase 0 fixes measurement honesty (U1 realistic April 2026 fills/costs and U2 tri-timestamp append-only quarantine of legacy ledgers), structural solvency (U3 ₹1,500–₹1,750 whole-lot risk cap, ₹3,500 portfolio-heat ceiling, dynamic NSE contract specs, and E−4 stock-option block), exit safety (U4 polarity-typed dual-stop kernel with Black-76 stress verification), and input integrity (U5 deny-by-default SmartTrading allowlist, transitive freshness TTLs, 09:18–14:45 entry / 15:10 EOD bounds, and strict Market Lens isolation)1.

### **Phase 1: Improve Evidence Quality and CIO Judgment**

Once Phase 0 passes verification and the 31-trade contradiction is forensically explained, deploy Upgrades **U6 through U12** under pre-registered protocol locks. Phase 1 compresses the MCP surface to \~32/18 high-signal fields free of Screener noise (U6), corrects options pricing to put-call-parity synthetic forward Black-76 (U7), hard-gates thin liquidity via rolling 5-second FRR ≤ 12% and DPR ≤ 0.25 (U8), eliminates numeric perception hallucinations and rupee-P\&L anchoring (U9), adds falsifiable post-loss cooldowns and 3-trade daily caps (U10), introduces Greek and Perold IS post-mortems (U11), and upgrades breadth and OI/GEX framing to reflect late-2026 Indian index structure honestly (U12)1.

### **Phase 2: Research-Only Experiments (Quarantined Offline)**

All Phase 2 experiments run strictly offline against recorded Phase 0–1 bitemporal ticks or shadow logs, never alter live paper packets without passing a pre-registered ablation gate, and satisfy all nine audit criteria below.

## **5\. Minimal Trade Decision Packet Specification**

To defeat long-context attention dilution20 and maintain strict trust boundaries between local deterministic controls and the external IDE-agent CIO, the MCP server should expose two compact, provenance-stamped packets. Raw full option chains, Screener fundamentals, unvalidated KOBP scores, and multi-day cumulative P\&L totals are deliberately excluded.  
![][image71]

### **Packet A: Pre-Entry Trade Decision Packet (\~32 Fields Maximum)**

The external IDE agent must inspect Packet A before proposing any entry. Whenever entry\_gate\_status is not OPEN, the local validator hard-rejects any action other than STAND\_ASIDE.

| Block | Fields | Units / Format | Provenance & Freshness Requirement | Authority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1\. Hard Gates (Top)** | Packet ID, Packet Timestamp (IST), Session Phase | UUID, ISO-IST, Enum (OPEN\_NORMAL / LOCKED) | Local NTP clock; OPEN\_NORMAL strictly 09:18–14:45 IST50 | Hard Gate |
|  | Entry Gate Status, Gate Block Reasons | OPEN / CLOSED\_STAND\_ASIDE, reason list | Deterministic rollup of feed TTL, cooldown, daily cap, and heat cap | Hard Gate |
|  | Remaining Daily Risk, Single-Trade Cap | ₹, ₹ | Append-only ledger (single-trade ≤ ₹1,750; daily ≤ ₹3,500) | Hard Cap |
|  | Trades Taken Today, Cooldown Remaining | Count (/3), Seconds | Persisted session behavioral state | Hard Cap |
|  | Open Positions Count, Portfolio Heat | Count (/2), ₹ | Realized daily loss \+ sum of open worst-case stressed risk | Hard Cap |
| **2\. Underlying & Micro-Regime** | Underlying, Expiry Date, Trading DTE | Symbol, YYYY-MM-DD, Days (float) | Daily NSE contract specification (Tuesday NIFTY weekly5) | Reference |
|  | Cash Spot LTP, Synthetic Forward, Futures Basis | Index pts, Index pts, Index pts | Parity median forward (age ≤ 1.5 s); flags PARITY\_ANOMALY1 | Advisory |
|  | Day Range % of 20-Day ATR, Session Range Position, Distance from 09:12 Pre-Open Equilibrium | %, 0%–100%, Index pts | Computed from licensed live broker bars \+ futures pre-open match (age ≤ 2 s)51 | Advisory |
|  | Top-10 Weighted Contribution (HCI₁₀), Breadth-Contribution Divergence (BCD) | %, \[−1, \+1\] | Quarterly NSE top-10 weights × live cash LTP vs. 50-stock A/D59 | Advisory |
|  | ATM Implied Volatility, Intraday ATM IV Change, India VIX | %, Vol pts, Index | Black-76 on synthetic forward (age ≤ 2 s)1 | Advisory |
| **3\. Slow Structural Context** | Call Wall Strike, Put Wall Strike, OI-Delta Age | Strike, Strike, Seconds | Intraday chain OI×Gamma; explicitly tagged PROVISIONAL27 | Advisory (Slow) |
|  | EOD Participant Net Sign, EOD As-Of Date | Client/Pro/FII summary, Date | NSE EOD participant-wise OI (T-1 trading day)28 | Advisory (Slow) |
|  | Overnight Gap, Scheduled Macro Event Flag | Index pts, Enum / Time | Pre-open futures equilibrium102 \+ pre-session event calendar | Advisory |

|  | Best Bid, Best Ask, Spread, Quote Age | ₹, ₹, ₹, ms | Live broker L1 (age ≤ 1,500 ms; fails closed if zero/crossed) | Hard Gate |
|  | L1 Bid Qty, L1 Ask Qty, L5 Book Imbalance | Units, Units, \[−1, \+1\] | Live broker L2 depth snapshot (age ≤ 1,500 ms) | Advisory / Gate |
|  | Delta, Gamma, Theta/Day, Vega/1% IV | Unit Greeks & ₹/lot | Black-76 on synthetic forward1 | Advisory |
|  | Modeled 1-Lot RT Friction, Rolling 5 s FRR, Rolling 5 s DPR | ₹, %, Ratio | April 2026 cost stack \+ rolling 5 s spread (hard gates: FRR ≤ 12%, DPR ≤ 0.25)1 | Hard Gate |

To initiate a paper trade, the external IDE agent must submit a structured **Entry Proposal** bound to Packet A containing: Packet ID (age ≤ 15 s), single-use UUID idempotency key, explicit action (STAND\_ASIDE or ENTER), contract symbol, direction (LONG\_CE or LONG\_PE), integer whole lots (≤ ![][image20]), cited ask price, cited synthetic forward, underlying-forward invalidation (index points, polarity-checked), option-premium catastrophic stop (₹/unit, stress-checked), forward target (index points), maximum hold duration (minutes, capped at 15:10 IST), and a structured setup/invalidation enum code rather than a free-form essay.

### **Packet B: In-Trade Management Packet (\~18 Fields Maximum, P\&L-Blind Framing)**

Inspected while holding an open position so the CIO can independently decide HOLD, TRAIL\_STOP (monotonic tightening only), PARTIAL\_BOOK (enabled only when open lots ≥ 2), or EXIT. Entry price, unrealized rupee P\&L, and multi-day cumulative P\&L are omitted to suppress disposition and sunk-cost anchoring63.

| Top-10 Weighted Contribution (HCI₁₀), Breadth Divergence (BCD), L5 Book Imbalance | %, \[−1, \+1\], \[−1, \+1\] | Summarizes live market confirmation or divergence from the present moment forward. |
| Allowed Stop Ratchet Bounds | Min new premium stop (₹); min (CE) or max (PE) underlying invalidation (pts) | Prints exact monotonic non-widening constraints enforced by the local kernel. |

## **6\. Rigorous Paper-Trading Evaluation Protocol**

Determining whether this cockpit plus an external IDE-agent CIO produces real net-of-cost edge—rather than luck, operator cherry-picking, stale-quote bias, or prompt overfitting—requires a pre-registered five-stage evaluation protocol governed by formal statistical power and multiple-testing penalties.  
![][image72]

### **Stage 1: Forensic Resolution of the 31-Trade Contradiction**

Before opening any qualifying validation epoch, conduct a one-time forensic diff of the legacy historical summary versus the 31-trade logic-test slice across six dimensions: fill model (LTP vs. bid/ask \+ costs), win rate vs. payoff ratio, exit-reason split (manual CIO exit vs. stop vs. EOD), underlying/expiry mix and India VIX regime, IDE model and prompt version, and quote staleness at decision time. Permanently quarantine both historical slices as **exploratory and non-qualifying**.

### **Stage 2: Pre-Registration and Anti-Selection-Bias Invocation Hygiene**

Before Trade 1 of a qualifying epoch, commit an immutable **Protocol Lock** fixing the IDE agent provider, model checkpoint ID, prompt hash, packet schema version, risk envelope (![][image43], ![][image73], cooldowns), and eligible strike universe. Any subsequent change increments a permanent global trial\_counter (![][image74]) and starts a new epoch. To eliminate human cherry-picking of *when* to summon the IDE agent, the primary qualifying track must invoke the agent on **fixed-clock checkpoints** (e.g., every 15 minutes from 09:20 to 14:35 IST) while logging 100% of STAND\_ASIDE decisions; any human-triggered ad-hoc invocation must be segregated into a separate AD\_HOC track rather than blended into the primary verdict.

### **Stage 3: Dual-Friction Scoring and Null-Hypothesis Benchmarks**

Score every closed qualifying trade across three parallel accounting tracks: (1) **Baseline Realistic 2026 Execution** (L2 bid/ask walk, 1.0 s latency, SL-L stop slippage, April 2026 statutory charges \+ brokerage1); (2) **Stressed 2× Friction Execution** (doubling spread/slippage drag and 2.0 s latency, reflecting the quantitative heuristic that an edge failing at 2× friction sits within cost-estimation noise88); and (3) **Three Null-Hypothesis Baselines** evaluated on identical timestamps—Zero-Expectancy Net-of-Costs (![][image75]), a Matched Random-Direction ATM benchmark with identical stops and EOD flatten (testing whether directional choice beats volatility/stop geometry), and a transparent mechanical session-open directional momentum baseline on synthetic forward (testing whether the IDE agent adds genuine discretionary value over a simple rule).

### **Stage 4: Non-Normal and Serial-Correlation-Safe Statistical Inference**

Compute per-trade net R-multiples (![][image76]) and daily net returns across at least **150 closed trades** spanning at least **40 trading days** and at least **2 distinct volatility/range regimes** (including both Tuesday expiry and non-expiry sessions45). Apply two mandatory tests: first, Bailey–López de Prado Minimum Track Record Length and Deflated Sharpe Ratio accounting for empirical skewness ![][image77], raw kurtosis ![][image78], and the full logged trial count ![][image74]15:  
![][image79]  
Extend sampling until ![][image80] and require DSR ≥ 0.951. Second, run a **10,000-draw Politis–Romano stationary bootstrap** on daily net returns using random geometric block lengths (mean block length 3–5 trading days) to preserve volatility clustering and intraday autocorrelation22, requiring the 95% lower confidence bound of daily mean return \> 0\.

### **Stage 5: Quantitative Promotion Versus Kill Thresholds**

| Evaluation Criterion | Kill / Fail (Halt & Redesign) | Inconclusive (Continue Sampling) | Promotion Gate (Eligible for Live-Mode Build & 1-Lot Soak) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Sample length & regime breadth | Early stop if N ≥ 50 and upper 95% CI of net expectancy \< 0, or drawdown \> 35% of ₹50k | N \< 150 trades or only 1 volatility regime | N ≥ max(150, MinTRL) across ≥40 trading days & ≥2 distinct regimes |
| Baseline net expectancy & Profit Factor | Net expectancy ≤ 0R or PF \< 1.05 | Expectancy 0–0.12R or PF 1.05–1.25 | Net expectancy ≥ \+0.15R and PF ≥ 1.30 net of April 2026 costs |
| Stressed 2× friction survival | Net P\&L negative (PF \< 1.00) | PF 1.00–1.10 | Profitable at 2× friction (PF ≥ 1.10 and expectancy \> \+0.05R)88 |
| Statistical significance (DSR & Bootstrap) | DSR \< 0.80 or stationary-bootstrap p \> 0.15 | DSR 0.80–0.95 | DSR ≥ 0.95 **and** stationary-bootstrap lower 95% CI \> 015 |
| Execution & payoff discipline | Realized payoff ratio \< 0.90 or fact-binding error rate \> 2% | Payoff ratio 0.90–1.10 | Payoff ratio ≥ 1.15, zero hard-gate breaches, IS within modeled budget |

## **7\. Critical Adjudication of the Seven Candidate Ideas**

None of the seven reviewer proposals should be accepted uncritically; two components should be explicitly **rejected** or **deferred**, and five require material redesign for late-2026 Indian F\&O microstructure and LLM reliability realities.

| Candidate Idea | Verdict | Technical Rationale and Required Disposition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1\. Structured, verifiable CIO thesis records** | **Accept Narrowly (Redesign — Drop Prose Essays)** | Machine-evaluable trade contracts (explicit forward invalidation, catastrophic premium stop, target, max hold time, and setup enum) add high attribution value. Free-form prose rationales must **not** be treated as verifiable evidence: NeurIPS 2023 (Turpin et al.) and Anthropic's May 2025 study show reasoning models frequently conceal true causal drivers in CoT (20%–29% faithfulness on misaligned hints, declining further on harder tasks)23. |
| **2\. Underlying-spot invalidation \+ option-premium catastrophic stop** | **Accept with Critical Redesign (Phase 0\)** | Essential concept, but hazardous in naive form for three NSE-specific reasons: (a) **Directional polarity:** option-premium stops are monotonically non-decreasing for *both* Long CE and Long PE, whereas underlying invalidation reverses polarity (non-decreasing floor for Long CE; non-increasing ceiling for Long PE)1; (b) **Spot vs. forward:** Indian index options price off synthetic forward/futures rather than cash spot, so ±30–120 pt basis shifts break spot-only triggers1; and (c) **Nonlinear drift & NSE stop rules:** 3 hours of flat-spot chop plus 1.5% IV crush can nearly exhaust the ₹3,500 cap before spot invalidates1, while NSE bans SL-M on options and enforces LPP (±40%/±₹20) and SL-L trigger-limit (20%/₹10) rejection bounds32. Implement per Upgrade 4\. |
| **3\. Frozen market-state snapshots at entry** | **Accept (Lean Schema Only — Phase 0\)** | Critical for deterministic replay, hindsight prevention, and fact-binding verification—provided snapshots freeze strictly the \~32-field decision packet plus raw candidate L1/L2 ticks and tri-timestamps, never bloated full-chain dumps. |
| **4\. Post-loss cooldown, re-entry controls, and trade-frequency caps** | **Accept with Counterfactual Guard (Phase 1\)** | Well grounded in Coval & Shumway's (2005) finding of post-loss afternoon risk escalation (+17.4% trades, \+9.5% size, \+27% adverse reversals)72 and SEBI's FY25–26 churn-loss data30. Must persist across restarts at the account level and log shadow counterfactuals so over-tight lockouts can be falsified (Upgrade 10). |
| **5\. MAE/MFE and friction post-mortems** | **Accept with Options Redesign (Phase 1\)** | Linear equity MAE/MFE (Sweeney93) fails on decaying convex options by conflating Delta direction with Theta bleed, IV crush, and basis drift. Upgrade into Taylor-Greek attribution plus Perold IS decomposition18, and ban mid-window stop curve-fitting (Upgrade 11). |
| **6\. Hash-chained audit records and "500-signal" snapshots** | **SPLIT: REJECT "500-Signal" Snapshots Permanently; DEFER Hash-Chaining to Live Mode** | **"500-signal" snapshots are actively destructive:** capturing 500 unvalidated signals invites post-hoc data-mining (exploding DSR multiple-testing hurdles42), raises engineering drag, and risks context-dilution leakage into the CIO19. **Cryptographic hash-chaining is premature in Phase 0–1:** on a single-user local paper cockpit, the binding risks are broken fill realism and silent database resets, not adversarial tampering. Use simple append-only bitemporal event sourcing now74, and defer hash-chaining to Live-Mode 5-year regulatory compliance (L5)33. |
| **7\. Automated fact-checking of an agent's stated evidence** | **SPLIT: ACCEPT Deterministic Numeric Binding (Phase 1); REJECT Semantic / Prose Checking** | Zero-LLM deterministic code confirming that the CIO's cited packet ID, strike, ask price, synthetic forward, stops, and max rupee loss match the frozen snapshot within ±1 tick is inexpensive and prevents perception hallucinations91 (Upgrade 9). Semantic or LLM-based checking of prose rationale is **rejected**: it conflicts with the no-LLM-API architecture, cannot catch unfaithful CoT24, and triggers Goodhart's Law reward hacking where the agent optimizes narrative compliance instead of net expectancy25. |

## **8\. The Five Most Dangerous Ways This Project Could Fool Its Operator**

> 1. **The Naive Paper-Fill and April 2026 Cost-Stack Mirage.** An illustrative 100-trade, 2-lot NIFTY option strategy earning \+₹29,120 (PF 1.27) under naive LTP paper fills collapses to −₹10,629 (PF 0.92)—or −₹36,467 (PF 0.75) under modest touch-fill bias—once post-April 2026 statutory charges (0.15% sell-side STT, 0.03553% NSE fees including IPFT, 18% GST, ₹20/order brokerage), bid-ask crossing, 1–2 s MCP latency, and SL-L stop slippage are deducted1. Without Upgrade 1, months of apparent paper profits can be pure accounting fiction.  
> 2. **Narrative Hypnosis from Eloquent but Unfaithful CIO Theses.** Frontier IDE agents generate crisp, institutional-sounding prose referencing gamma walls, breadth, and order flow even when their actual action was anchored on a prior turn, a noisy cue, or arbitrary tie-breaking23. Because empirical CoT faithfulness sits near 20%–29% on misaligned-hint evaluations and declines further on complex problems24, polished trade logs easily convince an operator that *verbal coherence* equals *statistical edge*.  
> 3. **Silent Multiple-Testing and Selective-Invocation Inflation ("P-Hacking by Conversation").** Iteratively editing prompts, swapping across Codex, Claude, and Antigravity, sidelining "bad logic-test slices," and summoning the IDE agent only when the operator intuitively likes a chart creates an uncounted search across dozens of configurations. Just 20 undocumented variants push the zero-skill expected maximum Sharpe hurdle to 0.152 per trade—erasing the apparent significance of a solid \+0.18R edge1—while disguising an irreproducible human-filtered loop.  
> 4. **False Safety from Spot-Anchored Stops and Uncorrelated Single-Trade Caps.** Displaying "max ₹3,500 single-trade risk" and "underlying spot invalidation" creates false comfort while masking three concrete hazards: (a) 7.0% risk per trade incurs a 23.3% probability of ≥50% drawdown even with a genuine \+0.125R edge1; (b) two concurrent correlated positions double simultaneous gap risk to ₹7,000 (2× the daily cap); and (c) three hours of flat-spot chop plus IV crush or a −30 pt futures basis shift can blow through the rupee risk ceiling before cash spot approaches invalidation1.  
> 5. **The "Paper-to-Live Switch" Execution Cliff on 2026 NSE Infrastructure.** Treating live readiness as a configuration toggle invites immediate operational failure. On late-2026 NSE infrastructure, API MARKET orders for emergency exits are pre-emptively blocked under NSE's algo market-order ban and April 2026 API-as-Algo routing34; SL-M orders are unavailable on options69; SL-L stops fail on LPP (±40%/±₹20) or trigger-limit (20%/₹10) rejections and sit unfilled across flash gaps32; broker REST timeouts77 trigger duplicate entries or accidental unhedged short reversals on retry without IN\_DOUBT reconciliation37; and holding single-stock options into the E−4 window triggers physical-delivery margin liquidation vastly exceeding ₹50,0006. Any live deployment that skips Prerequisites L1–L5 converts a bounded research cockpit into unhedged live-capital risk.
